description.narrative: The Fair, Green and Global Alliance (FGG) aims to increase the power and decision-making influence of organised, mobilised and informed civil society, especially women, to advance fair and green trade and value chains. FGG believes that poverty, inequality and exclusion are caused by power asymmetries. We see the unprecedented power of capital over people and planet as the primary obstacle impeding realisation of fair and green trade and value chains. The FGG programme focuses on recalibrating power within the global architecture of trade and value chains by amplifying the voices of targeted rights-holders – small producers and traders, workers, fishers, rural and Indigenous peoples, religious and ethnic minorities, and migrants, especially the women and youth among them – who are practising, claiming or defending human rights and fair and green economic practices, and/or whose rights are being ignored, threatened or violated by corporations and/or governments. We aim to transform social relations so that these rights-holders’ voices are heard and heeded. FGG’s eight members (ActionAid, Both ENDS, Clean Clothes Campaign, IT for Change, Milieudefensie/Friends of the Earth International/Friends of the Earth Europe, Samdhana Institute, SOMO and the Transnational Institute) cooperate with some 1000+ partners and allies in our many worldwide networks to strengthen collective capacities to advance a common vision of fair and green trade and value chains.

comment.narrative: In 2022, we aim for at least 2 instances, where a government institution from India will adopt our recommendations for governance of the digital economy and regulation of Big Tech corporations.

(1) IT for Change engaged with the UNESCO's effort to formulate a set of ‘Guidelines for Regulating Digital Platforms’ to safeguard freedom of expression and access to information in 2022. The revised draft of the guidelines has incorporated inputs forwarded by IT for Change, including, recognizing the impact of both platform content moderation and curation functions on freedom of speech and access to information, and makes a stronger reference to the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights to hold digital platforms accountable. These recommendations directly address key issues with respect to meaningful access to civic space in the online public sphere and emphasize stronger responsibilities on platform providers to guarantee a safe and violence-free communicative space for women and gender minorities. (x, g)

(1) Meta (formerly Facebook) (1), facing pressure from policy makers, civil society and users at large, rolled back a critical change to its data privacy policy with respect to Whatsapp, a move which in effect, would have given Facebook unparalleled control over user data and compromised the privacy of millions who use the service. IT for Change was part of a global campaign, Save Whatsaap, which worked with civil society and raised public awareness on this issue. (x)

We aim for at least 1 actor (likely a government body of the Government of India) to adopt our policy recommendations on digital economy regulation, that sets effective limits on corporate power, dissuades monopoly trends, improves corporate conduct and businesses, and /or contributes to ending data concentration in the digital economy.

comment.narrative: As a new member coming into an alliance with a ten year old history, learning has been a key priority for IT for Change in 2021. Through the year, we have had opportunities to use the FGG mandate to broaden understanding of the impacts of digitalization to value chains and global south development among our partners including unions and CSOs through multiple webinars, workshops, meetings and smaller discussions. IT for Change has also focused on broadening the understanding of these issues within the alliance through online learning sessions with FGG alliance members such as Centre for Research on Multinational Corporations (SOMO) and Transnational Institute (TNI) including a crash course on big tech and the Global South. In turn and equally, IT for Change has benefited from these interactions and been able to integrate critical insights and learnings from the work of partners and alliance members.

We will organize learning sessions on digital economy issues and their intersections with value chains for FGG consortium members as well as partner organizations.. We also view the opportunity to engage with long term partners as well as new members to our networks in the FGG program as a way to expand our learning with respect to issues, strategies and responses. Our work will be informed and modified by these collaborative processes.

IT for Change worked intensively on the goal of learning, capacity development and discourse widening around issues of digitalization within and outside of the FGG alliance. Through the year, we capitalized on the FGG mandate to broaden the understanding of the impacts of digitalization to value chains and Global South development among our partners including CSOs, unions and unions federations, government actors through webinars, workshops, and meetings. In addition to these, we specifically worked on learning initiatives that included: • DataSyn, our monthly newsletter is aimed at putting out informed analysis and debates on current issues of Big Tech, digital economy regulations, trade and e-commerce, gender in the digital economy, labor rights, food security, fintech and edtech and more. In 2022, we published 12 issues from over 30 contributors, reaching a readership base of 2700 readers in across 10 countries focussing on the above issues. The newsletter has served as important learning tool and accessible analysis for civil society organisations as well as strategically placed allies and advocates. • We brought out Platform Predicament - Making Sense of a Datafied Future of Work, a podcast series focusing on platform-based work, the rights of workers in platformised workplaces, and alternative, worker centric models for platform-based work. The goal of the podcast was to break down the conversation around platform-based gig work for platform workers, unions, researchers and practitioners. • We brought out the The State of Big Tech Compendium in 2022 on the theme of digital enclosures. This compendium has served as a significant advocacy and knowledge resource, and has been used by IT for Change in capacity development initiatives. As of December 31, 2022, the compendium has garnered over 8000 views. Some key essays were also cross posted by FGG alliance member TNI, in its State of Power Report in January 2023.Within the alliance, in 2022, we stepped up our learning efforts by contributing to pedagogic initiatives of alliance members, including an online course on digital capitalism by Transnational Institute. In 2022, FGG Alliance members SOMO, TNI, IT for Change and Samdhana came together came together to form a thematic working Group on Big Tech, Data Commons & Digital Trade Chapters, with the aim of converging efforts by alliance members on issues of digitalization. A core output that was seeded in the discussions was the development of a key baseline document/position paper, which can communicate and be a learning/advocacy tool with key actors. IT for Change also participated in interfaces with the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Dutch embassies in India sharing perspectives on digitalisation.

We will organize learning sessions on digital economy issues and their intersections with value chains for FGG consortium members as well as partner organizations. We also view the FGG mandate and our umbrella activities under the same, as an opportunity to engage in depth with long term partners and new members within our networks, whom we have cultivated via FGG on digital economy issues, and engineer cross learning and strategizing. We have been able to establish foundations towards this in 2022 and hope to build on the same in 2023.

description.narrative: process
lines of work in which FGG members and partners build upon gender analysis and incorporate gender justice in their strategy

comment.narrative: Gender justice is a critical component of all the work that we will be doing under the FGG program. Specifically, we will be focussing on research on women in digital value chains, gender and e-commerce, gender issues wrt women workers in the digital economy.

Gender justice is a critical component of all the work that IT for Change has undertaken under the FGG program. We have strived to bring concerns of gender justice into our policy work on e-commerce and Big Tech. Specifically, in 2022, we made headway in our ongoing research on women led MSMEs in digital value chains, with it now being in analysis and report writing stage. We also made headway in our advocacy efforts towards improved condition of women workers in the digital economy. Specific steps taken towards this have been 1) joining the gender and gig economy working group, a network of activists and scholars working towards the goal of a more gender just gig economy and 2) beginning our collaboration with the Asia Pacific Forum on Women, Law and Development. Further on the subject of India’s gig and platform economy, in our advocacy with NITI Aayog, the apex think tank of the Government of India, the issue of policy-making from a gender-sensitive lens became an important theme of the recommendations submitted.

Gender justice is a critical component of all the work that IT for Change has undertaken under the FGG program. We have strived to bring concerns of gender justice into our policy work on e-commerce and Big Tech. Specifically, we started exploratory work in 2021 on research on women led MSMEs in digital value chains, gender and e-commerce, and gender issues with respect to women workers in the digital economy. This compliments several lines of work that IT for Change has been pursuing focussing on the intersections of In 2021, we also had an exclusive focus on gender justice through our two-day online Institute on Feminist Perspectives on Digital Economy and Society which included participation from India, Philippines, Indonesia and Uganda.

A feminist standpoint and gender justice is integral to all of our strategies and will inform our work under the FGG mandate as well. In particular, our work will focus on the following themesa. women workers and producers in digital value chains; where we focus on gender just local to global rule making and policies that can improve and make more equitable terms of integration into the digital marketplace. We also see our work on improving corporate governance through competition, labor and taxation regulation inalienably tied to considerations of justice, equity and sustainability, all of which can contribute to better gender justice outcomes. b. Gender, digital trade and e-commerce - Through our networks and coalitions looking at the intersections of trade and gender, we will continue to counter current pink washing narratives within digital trade that simplistically present a neoliberal trade regime as the solution to women’s empowerment. Going beyond this, our work will attempt to widen discourse around e-commerce, women’s participation in the digital economy from a southern point of view.
